app.narrow_body: Local Eml is a desktop mail viewer and needs a wider window to lay out the library. Make the window larger or open it on a PC.
app.server_offline: Can't reach the local-eml server. Is it running?
app.temporary_banner: Temporary session: nothing is kept after you close this window.
app.temporary_banner_kept: Temporary session: this window's mail will be added to your library when you close it.

auth.title: Sign in to Local Eml
auth.body:
This browser has no session for the server on this port.
Open Local Eml from its launcher, or get a session token with the steps below.
auth.step_run: Copy this command, paste it there, and press Enter.
auth.step_paste: Copy the token it prints and paste it into the box above.
auth.open_windows: Press the Windows key, type cmd, then press Enter.
auth.open_mac: Press ⌘ Space, type Terminal, then press Enter.
auth.copy_failed: Couldn't copy. Select the command and copy it yourself.

library.title: Your library
library.body: Every message you've imported lives here. Click a subject to read it, or middle-click to open it in a new tab.

import.title: Import your mail
import.body: Drop .eml files, folders, .zip archives, .mbox files (Google Takeout) or Outlook .pst files here — or pull straight from an S3 bucket or IMAP mailbox. Duplicates are skipped automatically.

export.title: Export your library
export.body: Download everything as a single .zip, or upload to an S3 bucket. Re-running an export skips what's already there.

stats.title: Library stats
stats.body: See your archive in numbers: emails per year, top senders, total size, and more.

settings.title: Make it yours
settings.body: Switch the interface language, change date display, and manage saved IMAP and S3 profiles.

search.title: Search everything
search.body: Find messages by sender, subject, body or attachment name. Add filters like from:, has:attachment or after:2019 — the sliders button lists them all. Hangul initial consonants work too: type ㅎㄱ to find 한국.

starred.title: Star what matters
starred.body: Star messages from the list or the viewer, then use this filter to see only starred mail.

dates.title: Narrow by date
dates.body: Pick a start and end date to show only mail sent in that window. Both ends are included.

help.title: Need this again?
help.body: Press the question mark any time to replay this tour.

categories.title: Sort with categories
categories.body: Give mail a coloured label, then filter to it here. Create and rename categories under Settings → Categories; each email can carry one.

shortcuts.title: Keyboard shortcuts
shortcuts.body: Browse without the mouse: j/k move through the list, Enter opens, / jumps to search, and ←/→ step between emails in the viewer. Press ? anytime for the full list.

library.search_placeholder: Search mail, or try from: has:attachment…
library.table_caption: Email library. Select a subject to open the message.
library.new_mail_arrived: {count} new email arrived | {count} new emails arrived
library.selected_threads_hint: Actions apply to every message in the selected conversations.
library.bulk_delete_title: Delete {count} selected email? | Delete {count} selected emails?
library.bulk_delete_title_threads: Delete {count} selected conversation? | Delete {count} selected conversations?
library.bulk_delete_body: The messages and their .eml files are removed from this computer. This can't be undone. A full resync of the original source may import them again.

viewer.flag_menu: Flag as spam, phishing or safe
viewer.flag_banner: Flagged as {flag}. Shown as plain text only — HTML, images, attachments and links are disabled. Unflag it under Settings → Spam & phishing.
viewer.sha_help: The SHA-256 fingerprint of this message's .eml file. It uniquely identifies the message and is the file's name on disk.
viewer.no_html: No HTML part in this message.

external_link.title: Leaving Local Eml
external_link.body: This link goes to an external site and will open in a new tab.

missing_file.title: Message file is missing
missing_file.body: This message is listed in the database, but its .eml file can't be found on disk. It may have been deleted or moved outside Local Eml.
missing_file.question: Remove this entry from the database?

not_indexed.title: Not in the database
not_indexed.body: This .eml file is on disk but has no database entry, so it won't appear in the library or in search results. Add it now?

viewer.delete_body: The message and its .eml file are removed from this computer. This can't be undone. A full resync of the original source may import it again.

doc_preview.failed: This document couldn't be previewed. It may be password-protected or damaged. Download it to open it in its own app.
doc_preview.sheet_truncated: Showing the first {rows} rows and {cols} columns of {totalRows} × {totalCols}. Download the file to see everything.

import.drop: Drop .eml files, a directory, a .zip, an .mbox, or a .pst here
import.dedup_note: Duplicates are detected by SHA-256 and skipped.
import.s3_compat_hint: Leave blank for AWS. For MinIO, Cloudflare R2, Backblaze B2, Wasabi and similar, enter the service URL. Use http:// for a local MinIO.
import.s3_path_style_hint: Sends requests to <endpoint>/<bucket>. Turn on for MinIO and most self-hosted services.
import.s3_confirm_hint: Recursively imports every .eml object under the prefix.
import.profile_name_body: Shown on its card under Saved profiles, so you can load these settings again later.
import.profile_delete_body: Only the saved connection details are removed; nothing in the bucket or mailbox is touched.
import.s3_profile_select: Load this profile into the form below
import.s3_card_key_help: Only the key ID is saved. Enter the secret access key each time you use this profile.
import.s3_card_system_help: Uses ~/.aws/credentials or the AWS_* environment variables on this computer.
import.imap_hint: Connects read-only; messages are never marked read on the server.
import.imap_confirm_hint: Imports every message in the selected folder.
import.imap_sync_label: Receive new mail in the background
import.imap_sync_help: Stores the password encrypted on this machine. New mail comes in as soon as the server has it, if the server supports that, and is checked every {interval} either way.
import.imap_sync_help_off: Stores the password encrypted on this machine. Automatic fetching is turned off — use the interval below to enable it.
import.sync_interval_error: Failed to save the check interval
import.notify_label: Notify me when new mail arrives
import.notify_help: Shows a desktop notification when background sync brings in new mail, while Local Eml is open in a browser tab. Your browser asks for permission first.
import.notify_blocked: Notifications are blocked for this site. Allow them in your browser's site settings, then turn this on again.
import.notify_denied_toast: Notifications weren't allowed, so this stays off
import.notify_faq_intro: If notifications are on here but nothing pops up, your computer is usually holding them back. Check these settings, then send a test notification.
import.notify_faq_windows_1_body: Open Settings → System → Notifications and turn off "Do not disturb". While it's on, notifications go straight to the list without popping up.
import.notify_faq_windows_2_body: On the same page, open "Turn on do not disturb automatically" and clear the rules you don't want, such as when duplicating your display, when playing a game, or when using an app in full-screen mode.
import.notify_faq_windows_3_title: Turn on banners for your browser
import.notify_faq_windows_3_body: Still on that page, click your browser (Google Chrome or Microsoft Edge) under "Notifications from apps and other senders" and turn on "Show notification banners". If notifications show up in the list (Windows key + N) but never pop up, this is usually why.
import.notify_faq_mac_1_body: Open System Settings → Notifications, pick your browser (Google Chrome, Safari, Microsoft Edge or Firefox) and turn on "Allow notifications". Chrome may be listed as "Google Chrome Helper (Alerts)".
import.notify_faq_mac_2_body: On the same screen, set the alert style to "Banners" (they disappear by themselves) or "Alerts" (they stay until you close them). With "None", notifications only collect in Notification Center.
import.notify_faq_mac_3_body: If the Focus icon (a moon) is in the menu bar, notifications are held back. Turn Focus off in Control Center, or add your browser to the allowed apps under System Settings → Focus.
import.notify_faq_tab_note: The setting is under your browser's name, not Local Eml, because the browser shows the notification. Local Eml also has to be open in a tab.
import.notify_faq_test_off: Turn on "Notify me when new mail arrives" first.
import.imap_sync_needs_password: Run an import once to seed the password
import.imap_profile_select: Load this profile into the form below
import.imap_card_sync_toggle: Receive new mail in the background for {name}
import.imap_card_push_live_help: The server tells Local Eml the moment new mail arrives.
import.imap_card_push_retrying_help: The live connection dropped. Local Eml is reconnecting, and checks on the interval meanwhile.
import.imap_card_push_unsupported_help: This server can't announce new mail, so Local Eml checks for it on the interval.
import.imap_sync_help_cards: Turn it on for each profile with the switch on its card.
import.imap_sync_off_body: The saved password and sync position are removed. To turn it back on, run one import with the password again.
import.s3_creds_optional: Leave Access Key ID and Secret Access Key blank to use the credentials in ~/.aws/credentials or the AWS_* environment variables.

notify.enabled_body: You'll get a notification here when background sync brings in new mail.
notify.generic_body: Background sync brought in new mail.
notify.test_body: If you can see this, notifications are working.

export.zip_hint: Every .eml in your library is packed into one zip and streamed to your browser.
export.s3_hint: Streams every .eml to the bucket. Objects already at the destination prefix are skipped.
export.s3_confirm_hint: Uploads all local emails to the bucket under the given prefix; existing keys are skipped.

settings.flagged_help: Messages flagged as spam or phishing are hidden from the library and, when opened, shown as plain text only: no HTML, no images, no attachments, no clickable links. Unflag a message to restore it.
settings.risk_warnings_help: Checks each message offline for structural signs of phishing — links whose text doesn't match their destination, links to raw IP addresses or lookalike domains, failed SPF/DKIM/DMARC, a Reply-To on another site, executable attachments, password forms. It's a warning, never a verdict; nothing is hidden automatically.
settings.resync_help: Re-scans the .eml files on disk and adds any that are missing from the database. Existing messages are skipped.
settings.update_confirm: Local Eml {from} will be replaced with {to}. The download is verified against the release's SHA-256 checksums first. The server restarts and this page reloads by itself once it's back.
settings.date_format_help: Choose how dates are shown in the email list. The detail view always uses the full date.
settings.week_start_help: Which day begins the week in the date range calendar.
settings.attributions_intro: Local Eml is built with these open-source projects.
settings.attributions_full_hint: Copyright notices and license texts of every library and font included in this version.
settings.categories_help: Seven colour labels for organising mail, like Finder tags. Each email can carry one. Rename them here; leave a name blank to use the colour's own name.

stats.title: Library stats
stats.undated: {count} emails have no date and are not shown here.
stats.heatmap_hint: Sent time by weekday and hour, in your time zone.
stats.storage_hint: {size} of email, split into message text and attachments by type.
stats.empty: No emails yet — import some to see your stats.

attachments.title: Attachments
attachments.empty: No attachments yet. Attachments from the mail you import show up here.

shortcuts.title: Keyboard shortcuts
shortcuts.select: Tick / untick the email for bulk actions
shortcuts.prev_next: Previous / next email in the viewer

restore.title: Restore metadata from a backup
restore.hint: Upload an export .zip (or the local-eml.db inside it) to bring back stars, categories, settings and connection profiles. Import your .eml files first — the restore only applies metadata to emails already in the library, and never deletes anything.
restore.password_note: IMAP passwords cannot be restored: they are encrypted with a key that never leaves the original machine, so they are dropped from backups. Restored IMAP profiles come back with sync off — re-enter the password to re-enable it.
restore.confirm: Apply metadata from this backup? Stars, category assignments and settings in the backup overwrite current values.
restore.summary: {emails} emails updated · {categories} categories · {settings} settings · {profiles} profiles added

risk.title: This message has signs of phishing
risk.hint: Heuristic warning — check the sender and links before acting on it. Flag it to hide it and disable its links, mark it as not spam to silence this warning for this message, or turn warnings off under Settings → Spam & phishing.
risk.link_mismatch: Link text names a different site than it goes to
risk.ip_link: Link goes to a bare IP address
risk.reply_to_mismatch: Replies would go to a different site
risk.sender_mismatch: Display name embeds an address on another site

reading.title: Read tracking
reading.help: Keep track of which messages you have opened. Unread subjects are shown in bold, opening a message marks it read, and you can flip the state from the list or the viewer. Off by default; nothing changes until you turn it on.
reading.existing_title: How should your existing mail start?
reading.existing_body: Choose a starting state for everything already in your library. New messages arrive unread either way. You are only asked this once.
reading.mark_all_help: Useful after importing an archive or syncing a mailbox you had already read elsewhere.
reading.mark_all_confirm: Every message in your library will be marked read. Messages imported later still start unread.

privacy.temp_help: When this is on, every double-click launch starts with an empty library in a throwaway folder. Everything from that session is deleted when the app closes: mail, the search index, logs, and any profiles you saved. If the app crashes, the leftovers are removed the next time it starts.
privacy.temp_toggle_help: Takes effect from the next launch. The only thing kept on disk is a small file that remembers this switch.
privacy.temp_now: You're in a temporary session right now. Nothing from this window is kept after it closes.
privacy.temp_now_kept: You're in a temporary session right now. Because you chose to keep it, its mail will be added to your library when this window closes.
privacy.keep_toggle: Keep the mail from this window
privacy.keep_toggle_help: When this window closes, its mail, stars, read marks and categories are added to your library instead of deleted. Saved profiles come along without their passwords.
privacy.keep_now_on: The mail in this window will be added to your library when you close it.
privacy.temp_service: Not available while Local Eml runs as a background service, because the service never closes. To use a temporary session on this computer, stop the service or start Local Eml with --ephemeral.
privacy.enable_body: From the next double-click launch, Local Eml starts empty and deletes everything when it closes. This window keeps using your current library until then.
privacy.enable_wipe: Also delete my existing library now
privacy.wipe_help: Deletes every email, the search index, the import history and the logs. Background sync is turned off for saved IMAP profiles, so the mail doesn't come back on the next sync.
privacy.wipe_kept: Kept: saved IMAP and S3 profiles (without stored passwords), categories and settings.
privacy.wipe_confirm_body: This can't be undone. Type "{word}" to confirm.
privacy.key_keychain: Saved IMAP passwords are encrypted with a key kept in your system's secure storage: Windows Credential Manager, the macOS Keychain or the Linux secret service.
privacy.key_file: Saved IMAP passwords are encrypted with a key kept in a file only your account can read (keys/secret.key). Local Eml couldn't find secure storage it can use on this system, which is common on WSL, servers and containers.
privacy.key_keychain_unavailable: Saved IMAP passwords are encrypted with a key in your system's secure storage, but it isn't answering right now (it may be locked). Background sync can't sign in until it is unlocked. Local Eml keeps trying.
privacy.key_optout: To keep the key in a file instead, start Local Eml with LOCAL_EML_KEYRING=off. The key is moved back out of secure storage on that start.
privacy.disk_note: These options delete files the ordinary way. They are not secure erasure: deleted data may still be recoverable, especially on SSDs, and Local Eml can't restore it either. Keep a backup of anything you need. Provided as is, without warranty.

search_help.title: Search filters
search_help.intro: Plain words search the subject, people, body and attachment names. Combine them with any of these; click one to add it.

rows.subject: Words in the subject
rows.on: Sent on that day, month or year
rows.larger: Bigger than a size (K, M, G)
rows.exclude: Leave out mail with this word (works with filters too)
rows.category: In a category: its colour (red), its name, or none
rows.until: Sent on or before (includes that day)

search_help.dates: Dates can be a year (2019), a month (2019-03) or a day (2019-03-05). after:2019 before:2020 means all of 2019.

backup.title: Automatic backup
backup.hint: Copies your mail into a folder on a schedule. Use an external drive, a NAS, or a folder that Dropbox, OneDrive or Google Drive syncs. Each backup copies only new mail, and nothing is ever deleted from the folder, so mail you delete here stays in the backup.
backup.folder_hint: The full path of a folder on this computer. It is created if it doesn’t exist.
backup.last_ok: Last backup {when}: {added} new message copied, {total} in total. | Last backup {when}: {added} new messages copied, {total} in total.
backup.some_failed: {count} messages couldn’t be copied; see the log for details.
backup.schedule_daily: Runs about once a day while Local Eml is running. A missed backup runs soon after it next starts.
backup.schedule_weekly: Runs about once a week while Local Eml is running. A missed backup runs soon after it next starts.
backup.temporary: Backups are off in a temporary session.

duplicates.help: The same email can end up in your library twice when it comes in two ways, for example from a Google Takeout .mbox and again through IMAP. Copies are matched by their Message-ID and date. Merging keeps one copy and deletes the others, and anything you did to any copy carries over: stars, read state and category.
duplicates.summary: {groups} emails are stored more than once: {extra} extra copy using {size}. | {groups} emails are stored more than once: {extra} extra copies using {size}.
duplicates.merge_all: Remove {count} extra copy | Remove {count} extra copies
duplicates.merge_one: Keep one, remove {count} | Keep one, remove {count}
duplicates.merge_page: Merge every group on this page
duplicates.empty: No duplicates. Every email in your library is stored once.
duplicates.merged: Removed {count} extra copy. | Removed {count} extra copies.
duplicates.confirm_title: Remove {count} extra copy? | Remove {count} extra copies?
duplicates.confirm_body: Each email keeps its oldest import. Stars, read state and categories move to the copy that stays. The other copies and their .eml files are deleted, and this can’t be undone.

format.zip_hint: One file per message, plus index.csv listing them all.
format.mbox_hint: Opens in Thunderbird, Apple Mail or another Local Eml.
format.pdf_hint: Every message in one printout, with a contents page.

export_selection.too_many_to_print: Printing is limited to {max} messages. Narrow the search, or export a .zip instead.

saved_search.empty: No saved searches yet. Search for something, then save it here.
saved_search.save_disabled: Type a search or pick a filter to save it
saved_search.dialog_body: Saves “{query}” so you can open it again with one click.
saved_search.delete_body: This removes “{query}” from your saved searches. Your mail isn’t affected.
